sectors.name: Technology
themes: Indonesia's digital economy grows independently of US tech cycles, driven by rising domestic e-commerce penetration and government-backed digital infrastructure spending.
Local platform winners like BELI and BUKA benefit from structural shifts in consumer behavior, including rural adoption and cashless payments, insulating them from global rate volatility.
US-listed tech names remain vulnerable to higher-for-longer rates and AI capex digestion, making them tactical shorts or underweights versus Indonesian counterparts with stronger relative momentum.
sectors.ai: Buy selective Indonesian tech names with local revenue exposure (BELI, IRSX, BUKA) as US-listed peers drag on sentiment; the +0.92% ID vs -2.22% US spread confirms domestic resilience. Rotate out of US-exposed cyclicals, add to e-commerce and digital infrastructure leaders on pullbacks, and trim positions ahead of any global risk-off spike.

Regulatory tailwinds for sharia-compliant and micro-lending products are creating durable niches, lifting BGTG, BBLD, and TRJA as domestic liquidity rotates into specialized lenders.

Favor small-cap insurers and multi-finance names with strong momentum; trim US-sensitive banks. Position for continued ID outperformance over 1-2 months, targeting +5-8% upside on leaders.

themes: Indonesia's coal export demand remains structurally supported by China's thermal coal import quotas and India's rising power demand, sustaining volume growth for large-cap producers like BUMI.

Energy sector volatility is amplified by domestic retail participation in small caps, creating frequent mispricings that institutional investors can exploit via liquidity-focused entry points.
sectors.ai: Buy selective exposure to coal and nickel names with confirmed volume and earnings momentum (BUMI, CUAN) while avoiding speculative small caps (SQMI, ALKA) that show unsustainable spikes. Position for Q3 coal price support from Chinese restocking and Indonesia's downstream nickel policy; trim on any breach of IDX energy support.

themes: Indonesia's universal health coverage (JKN) expansion continues to drive volume growth for hospital chains and pharmaceutical distributors, insulating them from global macro swings.
Domestic healthcare names benefit from a young, growing middle class with rising out-of-pocket spending on private care, a durable tailwind absent in mature US markets.
Regulatory support for local vaccine and generic drug manufacturing (e.g., NOVN, DKHH) is accelerating import substitution, creating structural margin expansion opportunities.
sectors.ai: Buy dips in Indonesian hospital operators (HEAL, SAME) and pharma distributors (DKHH) as domestic healthcare demand outpaces US peers; AIMS' +25% spike is speculative—take profits. Rotate into NOVN for vaccine upside. Maintain neutral US exposure; MRNA/CVS rallies are sentiment-driven, not structural.

themes: DeFi infrastructure tokens (UNI, CRV, SKY) are outperforming as on-chain activity and fee-generation models gain structural adoption, independent of Bitcoin's price direction.

Stablecoin and yield protocols (ENA, MORPHO, JST) benefit from rising global rates and institutional treasury allocations, making them resilient even in low-volatility crypto regimes.
sectors.ai: Rotate into DeFi and storage plays (FIL, UNI, CRV) on relative strength while global crypto aggregates drift flat; the signal is normal, so avoid adding beta.
